processes.description: The Transwestern commercial team plans its strategy through meetings called by the director or an assistant: group direction and yearly goals, plus project and customer sessions such as a storage project, the Window Rock interconnect with Burlington, lost customers to win back and the fuel charge on the Sun Devil project. Staff bring supporting material to these sessions, such as pipeline expansion cases, energy estimates for new plants and the proposals sent to customers. The sessions decide negotiation positions and who will market to new loads.
steps: A manager or assistant calls a strategy meeting, or a staff member asks for one on a project or customer.
The meeting time and room are set and often moved by the assistant.
Staff gather supporting material: expansion cases, plant energy estimates, earlier customer proposals.
The material is forwarded to the group before the meeting.
The group meets to settle direction, negotiation parameters and who covers which customer.
Follow-up meetings with customers or partners are arranged.

stalls.summary: A strategy request reached the wrong person and had to be redirected before anyone could respond.
A staff member could not proceed on a project negotiation without being told the fuel charge parameters, and the team had to seek a volunteer to market to a new power plant.
An outside party cancelled a planned meeting, so the discussion had to be rearranged.

automation.approach: Keep a shared strategy pack per project or customer: a standing agenda, the current expansion cases, open proposals and agreed negotiation parameters in one place, so each meeting starts from the same updated material instead of forwarded attachments.
automation.rationale: Most rounds rebuild the same background (cases, proposals, customer status) for a meeting. A standard strategy-pack layout cuts that preparation, while the judgement in the meeting stays with the team.

work_estimate.rationale: Time goes to preparing material for the meeting: running or pulling expansion cases, estimating plant energy needs, collecting past proposals, and scheduling the room. Some rounds are a calendar notice only, others need real analysis, hence the wide range. Only gathering and formatting the pack can be templated.

processes.description: Each mid-year and year-end cycle, announced by HR with a schedule, managers ask staff to choose reviewers and list their accomplishments, staff send reviewer names and accomplishment bullets, reviewers write feedback, and managers hold a PRC meeting to rank people. Managers then write reviews on the PEP form, get signed copies back and communicate results, sometimes handling objections about who should review whom or how a rating was reached.
steps: HR announces the performance cycle and its schedule.
Managers ask staff to pick reviewers, entered in the PEP system or sent by email.
Staff submit their accomplishments and reviewers write feedback.
The manager schedules and holds the PRC meeting to rank staff.
The manager writes each review on the standard form and discusses it with the employee.
Signed copies are collected and filed.

stalls.summary: The PEP system had problems, so reviewer lists had to be sent by email to the manager instead.
Accomplishments and reviews arrived late or needed chasing, including a manager asking for word on a pending review.
Submissions came back in the wrong form: a manager wanted an outline of duties rather than goals and accomplishments.

contradictions.summary: The same manager set the PRC meeting for one Thursday and later reminded staff it would be held on a Tuesday the following week.
Reviewer selection was to be done in the PEP system, but another instruction told staff to email reviewer lists to the manager instead.

automation.approach: Use a cycle checklist with fixed dates for reviewer selection, accomplishments, feedback, PRC and signed copies, plus a standard accomplishments form that asks for duties and results, so managers track who is outstanding in one view.
automation.rationale: The rounds repeat the same sequence and the stalls are late or misformatted submissions and a fallback when the system failed. A checklist with a standard form makes each stage and its owner clear; the writing and ranking remain people's work.

work_estimate.rationale: Time goes to compiling accomplishment lists, choosing reviewers, writing feedback or a review on the PEP form, and preparing for the PRC ranking. A reviewer list takes little, a written review and its discussion far more, so the range is wide. Collecting submissions and tracking status could be automated; the assessment cannot.

processes.description: The real-time desk sends the daily EES and El Paso Electric models and hourly data files to customers and settlements, forwarding them on and keeping the recipient list current. Desk staff also reconcile the El Paso model against the internal CARP report each month and complete a monthly EPE reconciliation sheet.
steps: The desk prepares the daily real-time model for EES or EPE for the prior day.
The model is emailed to the distribution list and forwarded where needed.
Recipients are added or removed from the list when staff change.
Hourly data are added to the daily mail-out on request.
The real-time model is reconciled against the CARP report and the monthly reconciliation sheet is completed.

stalls.summary: Files went to the wrong Bill Williams because of a name clash, so the sender had to confirm the correct recipient.

automation.approach: Generate and send the daily model from the scheduling system to a maintained distribution list, and run an automatic comparison of the real-time model against the CARP report that flags only variances for review.
automation.rationale: The work is a fixed daily send and a periodic reconciliation. A short procedure covering the file, the list owner and the reconciliation check keeps it consistent, and most of the send and comparison can be scripted.

work_estimate.rationale: Most rounds are a daily model saved and attached for the prior day; some add list maintenance, and the reconciliation round needs a check of several days against the CARP report. Producing and comparing files is mechanical, so much of it could be scripted, with people reviewing variances.
